clue.text: Superlatively poor connection to a TV programme

blocks.note: first meaning: the least strong link in a chain, poor in the highest degree
second meaning: the BBC quiz show hosted by Anne Robinson

explanation.surface: Someone grumbles about a terrible signal while trying to watch a television show.
explanation.walkthrough: The Weakest Link was a BBC quiz where contestants voted off the weakest player each round; 'Superlatively' points to the -est form.
explanation.definitionFit: The quiz title is literally the phrase for the feeblest joint in a chain.

clue.text: Drink to Mexican spirit at dawn

blocks.note: the agave spirit of Mexico
dawn is when the sun comes up

explanation.surface: A toast raised to the national spirit of Mexico as the sun comes up.
explanation.definitionFit: A Tequila Sunrise is a cocktail of tequila, orange juice and grenadine, named for its layered colours.

clue.text: Teed off, involving teams that were already there

indicators.note: something gone off has spoiled and changed, so the word teed is rearranged
to involve is to take in, so the jumbled letters wrap around another piece

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
a football or cricket team is an eleven, written XI in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: Golfers teed off with teams that had already turned up at the course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Teed off' reads as a golf phrase, but 'off' is the anagram signal. A team of eleven players is written XI, so teams are XIS.
explanation.definitionFit: Existed is past tense for having being, so things that existed were already present in the world.

clue.text: Rinse some knitting for the sake of appearances

indicators.note: knitting loops and interweaves strands, so the letters are worked into a new pattern

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone washes a bit of their knitwear just to keep up appearances.
explanation.definitionFit: An emersion is an emerging or coming into view, as of a star after eclipse, so a showing or appearance.

clue.text: Fictional knave with bird

blocks.note: surface reading: a rogue in a story who keeps a pet bird
setter's reading: the hawk in Barry Hines's novel A ... for a Knave, trained by the boy Billy Casper

explanation.walkthrough: Barry Hines's novel A Kestrel for a Knave, filmed as Kes, follows a Yorkshire boy who trains a young kestrel.
explanation.definitionFit: The bird belonging to the novel's knave is the small falcon of its title.

clue.text: Hebrew prophet, captured by clandestine army unit, is given some Indian food

indicators.note: a captive is held inside by its captor, so one piece goes within the other

blocks.note: the Special Air Service, the British special forces regiment
Amos is a minor prophet of the Old Testament

explanation.surface: An Old Testament prophet, seized by special forces, is handed some curry-house snacks.
explanation.definitionFit: Samosas are fried pastry triangles filled with spiced vegetables or meat, a staple snack of Indian cuisine.

clue.text: Redhead follows student, one that's friendless

definitions.note: the answer is a noun; the clue's adjective describes such a person

indicators.note: the head of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

blocks.note: L is the learner plate on a student driver's car
taken as written
the head, or opening letter, of red

explanation.surface: A red-haired newcomer trails behind a student, the one who has no friends.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redhead' looks like a person; it means the first letter of red, which follows L and ONE.
explanation.definitionFit: A loner is a person who avoids company and so goes without companions.

clue.text: Get less than 50% and still sound mighty pleased!

blocks.note: first meaning: falling short of one half
second meaning: a British exclamation of hearty agreement, roughly 'very much so!'

explanation.surface: A student scores under half marks yet still seems thrilled about it.
explanation.walkthrough: In British speech 'Not half!' is an emphatic yes, as in 'Did you enjoy it? Not half!'
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase literally denies reaching one half, while idiomatically it expresses strong enthusiasm.

clue.text: Short meeting that was filmed

definitions.note: a description of the answer, the title of a film

blocks.note: brief means short
an encounter is a meeting

explanation.surface: A quick get-together that someone caught on camera.
explanation.walkthrough: Brief Encounter is David Lean's 1945 film of Noel Coward's play about a fleeting romance at a railway station.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a classic British film, so the short meeting is one that was put on screen.

clue.text: Shakes those holding the weapons

blocks.note: first meaning: trembles
second meaning: cases that hold an archer's arrows

explanation.surface: People tremble in fear of armed men.
explanation.definitionFit: The verb means trembles slightly, while the noun names an archer's case for carrying arrows.

clue.text: Screen watchdog

blocks.note: first meaning: a computer display
second meaning: someone who oversees and checks up on others

explanation.walkthrough: 'Screen watchdog' reads like a censor for films; the two words are separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a display unit for a computer and an official who supervises or keeps watch.

clue.text: Tiny mites of 10 sat facing backwards

indicators.note: turning to face the other way means the word sat is read from its end

blocks.note: the figures 1 and 0 look like the letters I and O
taken as written, then turned round

explanation.surface: Ten little creatures sitting with their backs turned.
explanation.walkthrough: '10' is not a cross-reference here: its digits are read as the letters I and O.
explanation.definitionFit: Mite here means a very small amount, and an iota is the smallest Greek letter, so a jot.

clue.text: About an expert at riding the waves getting to come to the top again

blocks.note: re means about, concerning
to surf is to ride the waves
an ace is an expert

explanation.surface: Talk of a champion surfer who keeps popping back up out of the water.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Expert at riding the waves' is read as ACE at SURF, and the pieces run RE, SURF, ACE.
explanation.definitionFit: To resurface is to rise back up to the surface of water after being under it.

clue.text: Censor lad mistakenly for being a lion tamer

indicators.note: done mistakenly means put together wrongly, so the letters come out in a new order

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A boy is wrongly reprimanded for working as a lion tamer in the circus.
explanation.walkthrough: In the fable, Androcles pulls a thorn from a lion's paw, and the grateful lion later spares him in the arena.
explanation.definitionFit: The runaway slave of the legend befriended and calmed a wild lion, so he is a loose example of a lion tamer.

clue.text: Daniel wrote of retreating into the river

definitions.note: names the writer Daniel, author of Robinson Crusoe

indicators.note: retreating means going back, so the little word of is read backwards
going into something puts it inside, so one piece sits within the river

blocks.note: first part of the Dee, a river in Cheshire and Wales
taken as written, then turned round
last letter of the Dee

explanation.surface: A writer called Daniel describes retreating into a river.
explanation.walkthrough: The Dee is a river in Wales and Cheshire; reversed OF goes into it.
explanation.definitionFit: Daniel Defoe was the English novelist who wrote Robinson Crusoe and Moll Flanders.

clue.text: Tell four to note the order

blocks.note: to direct someone is to tell them what to do
four in Roman numerals
E is a note of the musical scale

explanation.surface: A boss instructs four staff to take note of the command.
explanation.definitionFit: A directive is an official instruction, a command issued by an authority.

clue.text: You and I, the Queen's employers

blocks.note: you and I together are us
ER is Elizabeth Regina, so the Queen's is ER'S

explanation.surface: We two are the people who employ staff for Her Majesty.
explanation.walkthrough: ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the crossword Queen; the possessive adds the S.
explanation.definitionFit: People who employ something put it to use, so employers in that sense are those who use it.

clue.text: Ban imposed to bag more hash

indicators.note: to make a hash of something is to mess it up, so the letters are scrambled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A prohibition was brought in to stop dealers bagging up more cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hash' looks like the drug, but it means a mess, signalling the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially one placed on trade with a country.

clue.text: Is cry a bit unusual, smacking of self-indulgence?

indicators.note: unusual means out of the normal order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone wonders whether having a little weep is somehow indulgent.
explanation.walkthrough: Sybaris was an ancient Greek city famed for its luxury, which gives the word.
explanation.definitionFit: Sybaritic describes a love of luxury and pleasure, so it suggests excessive self-indulgence.

clue.text: Faster bird about to rise

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means reading upwards, so the word for about runs backwards

blocks.note: the swift is a fast-flying bird
re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A quicker bird is about to take off.
explanation.definitionFit: Swifter is the comparative of swift, meaning quicker or more rapid.

clue.text: Headgear for group on French water

blocks.note: a band is a group, of people or musicians
eau is French for water; 'on' places it after

explanation.surface: Hats for a party going out on a French lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bandeau is a narrow band worn around the head to hold the hair, a type of headwear.

clue.text: Stations to name in one

blocks.note: a term is a name or word for something
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: Railway stations told to be named as a single entity.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' looks like a container signal but is simply part of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Termini are end-of-line railway or bus stations, the plural of terminus.

clue.text: Disobedient cat in revolt

blocks.note: rebel used as an adjective for defiant
the lion is a big cat

explanation.surface: An unruly cat is rising up against its owners.
explanation.definitionFit: A rebellion is an armed uprising against authority, the same thing as a revolt.

clue.text: Hanger-on finds shelter in front of church

blocks.note: the lee is the sheltered side, away from the wind
CH is the abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A sponger takes refuge outside a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A leech is a bloodsucking worm, and figuratively a parasite who clings to others for gain.

clue.text: Island copper goes round for suspect

indicators.note: a suspect account is not to be trusted as given, so the letters are rearranged
going round something encloses it, so one piece wraps another

blocks.note: Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A policeman on an island circles round a suspect.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Copper' looks like a policeman, but it is the metal, symbol Cu.
explanation.definitionFit: Corfu is a Greek island in the Ionian Sea, off the coast of Albania.

clue.text: Hesitation seen in exhausted reptile

indicators.note: something seen in a thing is inside it, so one piece is placed within another

blocks.note: spent means worn out
er is the sound of hesitating

explanation.surface: A worn-out snake pauses uncertainly.
explanation.definitionFit: A serpent is a snake, and snakes are reptiles.

clue.text: Noel, it is thought, is partly one of those who believes in top people

definitions.text: one of those who believes in top people

indicators.note: partly means only a portion is used, so the answer lies within the run of words

blocks.note: the letters run across noel, it, is and thought

explanation.surface: Noel's opinion is, in part, that of a snob who favours the upper class.
explanation.definitionFit: An elitist believes society should be led by a select, superior few.

clue.text: Head of order found, in error, the soup I'm stirring

indicators.note: stirring mixes things up, so these letters are blended into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written, part of the letters to be mixed
taken as written, the rest of the letters to be mixed

explanation.surface: A convent's leader admits she stirred the soup wrongly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in error' looks like the anagram signal, but error is part of the fodder; stirring does the mixing.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mother Superior is the nun in charge of a convent, the head of a religious order.
